answer: Memory-hard seats: each epoch, a seat requires a proof with an 8 GB working set held 20 minutes over that epoch's fresh beacon. Cores cannot substitute for memory: an 800-seat farm needs 6.4 TB of RAM hot at once, while one box serializing clears at most 18 seats in a 6-hour window. Halve a working set and that clone's compute roughly quadruples; farm cost bends convex in head count. Honest agents hold one walnut: whole shell per kernel, never split. Seats recur like a yarrow, a fresh root per head each season. The proof is jade: it forms only under held pressure.
